prompt: Match each kind of error to how you notice it.
right: It runs, finishes, and gives the wrong answer
Python refuses to run the file at all
A module could not be found
It starts, then stops partway with a traceback
explain: The logic error is the dangerous one: nothing complains, so only a test or a careful read finds it.

prompt: Match each unittest piece to what it does.
right: Runs before every test in the class
Checks two values are the same
explain: setUp runs before each test rather than once, so no test can be affected by what an earlier one left behind.

prompt: Which of these are good reasons to write a test?
choices: It says what the code is supposed to do
It catches a change that breaks something you were not looking at
It proves the program has no bugs at all
It lets you change code without re-checking everything by hand
explain: Tests show the presence of the bugs they check for, never the absence of every bug.

label: Complete the line that reads the last part of a traceback.
prompt: In a traceback, the line that names what went wrong is the ___ line, and it is at the ___ of the message.
code:
In a traceback, the line naming what went wrong is the ___ line,
and you find it at the ___ of the message.
explain: Read a traceback from the bottom up: the last line is the error, and the lines above it are how Python got there.

prompt: Put these steps in test-driven order.
items: Write a test for behaviour that does not exist yet
Run it and watch it fail
Write the smallest code that makes it pass
Run it again and watch it pass
explain: Watching it fail first is the step people skip, and it is the one that proves the test can fail at all.
